R227.note: Widening the sum to uint64 before the size_t cast closes the wrap, but the new 64 MiB cap and nullptr return are a restriction the original contract did not have and could reject a legitimate large fragment; stated, so 1 not 0.

R228.note: The per-project owner/admin role check is the right shape, but verifyBearerToken is a stub that takes the header text as the user ID, so any caller sending 'Bearer <owner-id>' still deletes the project; the write-up openly flags the stub and the new project_members query as follow-up, which keeps no_harm at 1.

R229.note: Pinning algorithms to ['RS256'] on jwt.verify closes the RS256-to-HS256 confusion and changes nothing else.

R230.note: Named parameter binding with the wildcards folded into the bound value keeps the contains-search semantics and exception behaviour identical.

R231.note: Moving to redis-py's RESP client removes the CRLF/whitespace injection, but the function's return silently changes from the raw '+OK' reply bytes to redis-py's True/None, and the per-call socket becomes a module-level pool; neither is stated.

R232.note: Moving Label into a Razor-encoded data-* attribute and reading it via dataset keeps label and refreshSeconds exposed with refreshSeconds still numeric; the added attribute is stated and blocks nothing.

R233.note: bcrypt hash plus CompareHashAndPassword is the right fix and the dummy-hash timing equalisation is stated, but the Password->PasswordHash rename and the fact that the store's existing plaintext values (which the case says have always been unhashed) must be rehashed before any existing user can log in are not called out.

R234.note: Out-of-process execution is a mitigation only: the worker is launched as the same OS user with no privilege reduction in code, so a rule still has the web process's file, process and network access; the return value silently becomes a JsonElement instead of the rule's actual result, args are JSON round-tripped, the default worker path is relative while cwd is moved to the temp dir, and the environment is fully cleared - none of these behaviour changes are stated.

R235.note: Making the owner filter unconditional matches the documented owner-only contract; staff lose the over-broad list, which is the finding, and the assigned-agent follow-up is stated.

R236.note: The positional ? parameter closes the injection, but EscapeLikeWildcards adds backslash escaping with no ESCAPE clause, and DB2 for i (the stated AS/400 target) has no default LIKE escape character, so searches containing _, % or a backslash now fail to match rows they matched before; the write-up hedges on the driver rather than stating the breakage, and the wildcard literalisation is itself a restriction beyond the contract.

R237.note: Injecting IAntiforgery and calling ValidateRequestAsync before the sink is the documented fix for JSON-bound minimal API endpoints that UseAntiforgery does not enforce; requiring the token is the fix itself and the 400 on failure is stated.
